main_system_reason: It is the only plan of Rojdi with a north arrow and measurable walls; the north wall, the longest and straightest, carries most of the weight.
notes: Rojdi is a village settlement with rubble-stone architecture. We measured the one plan in Possehl and Raval (1989) that has both a north arrow and long walls: Fig. 23, the Subphase 2b building on the Main Mound. Its walls are irregular rubble and its walls spread over about twenty degrees, the eastern wall being the most oblique, so the scatter is large and the result describes one building rather than a town layout. The plans of the South Extension (Fig. 18) and the Large Square Building (Fig. 17) carry the excavation grid but no north arrow, and the Gujarat State Department of Archaeology's site plan (Fig. 27) shows the mound outline only; none was measured.
